name: @shepherd/ext-github
description: shepherd.github — the pull requests a task has open, where its agents are.
//exports: The split every extension makes: main imports ./manifest to register, the utility process imports the root (which pulls in `activate`), ./model is the pure layer, and ./ui is the half the renderer mounts.
//dependencies: @shepherd/ext-tasks is TYPE-ONLY — `import type` and nothing else. The runtime relationship is the point id plus the manifest's `dependencies` entry, which is the gate the host can review; a value import would route around it. See extensions/README.md.
//octokit: @octokit/rest is a plain npm dependency, not a workspace one: the boundary lint is about which SHEPHERD packages an extension may reach, and a vendor client is exactly the kind of thing an extension is supposed to own privately. It is the only place in the repo that knows GitHub's wire shapes.
//shepherd: The manifest, as an extension declares it. `src/manifest.ts` is the typed copy the host loads, and `manifest.test.ts` asserts the two are identical.

secrets.title: GitHub token
secrets.description: Only needed if `gh auth token` cannot answer — this extension asks the GitHub CLI first. A fine-grained token with read access to pull requests is enough; add write to merge from here.

//ui: The UI half, imported ONLY by the renderer (boundaries.js). A separate subpath because it is a separate PROCESS: `.` is the service half and runs in a utility process with no DOM.
